name: Battle Party
description: Which owned creatures are active in the current battle, and which healthy party member must replace a defeated one. pets.team_composition owns the durable party and storage boxes; this owns only encounter-scoped active slots and switching. A voluntary switch is a battle command, while a knockout replacement is a forced decision that does not get silently auto-picked unless the host configures that policy. When no usable replacement remains it emits pets.partyDefeated, giving combat.command_round one authoritative loss signal. It owns no party membership, capture odds, damage or turn ordering, which keeps storage, combat math and sequencing in their existing components.

inputs.name: activeSlotsPerSide
inputs.description: Active creatures per side. One gives the classic single encounter; two enables double battles without changing party storage.

inputs.name: allowVoluntarySwitch
inputs.description: Whether a player may spend a command replacing an active creature with a healthy party member.

inputs.name: automaticReplacement
inputs.description: Whether the first healthy replacement is selected after a knockout. False emits the replacement requirement and waits for input.

outputs.name: activeBySide
outputs.description: Encounter side to active creature ids. Membership remains owned by Team Composition.

outputs.name: availableReplacements
outputs.description: Healthy, non-active party creatures eligible for a voluntary or forced switch.

outputs.name: replacementRequiredFor
outputs.description: Side that must choose a replacement, or empty when no forced decision is pending.

provenance: Added 2026-11-02 for the Pokémon battle-and-capture extraction. Searched party and roster ownership first: pets.team_composition stores the durable party and boxes, social.party_formation positions player characters, and combat.unit_roster tracks units already on an encounter board. None maps owned creatures to active battle slots or handles voluntary switching and forced knockout replacement. Library-native; this is encounter-scoped active-party state, not another ownership roster.
